answer: Each agent earns influence through a time-locked stake in a shared vault, and can withdraw only after a public cooling-off period. The protocol caps voting weight per verified stake unit and slashes funds when an agent signs conflicting transactions, so creating many identities does not multiply influence without multiplying capital. A sybil operator must lock real assets for each identity, leave them exposed to penalties, and wait to recover them; splitting stake buys no shortcut to the harbor. Even a sonnet of persuasive profiles cannot erase that cost.
